title: Fixed verbs: past and order
blurb: Every past verb and every order verb is fixed. Learn all their forms and what they are built on.

data.title: Two kinds of verb that never change
data.text: A past verb and an order verb are always fixed. Their ending tells you who did the action, and it never moves for iʿrāb.

blocks.html:
STAGE 3 · UNIT 6

Two kinds of verb that never change

A past verb and an order verb are always fixed. Their ending tells you who did the action, and it never moves for iʿrāb.

الفِعْلُ المَبْنِيُّ

data.text: Arabic has three kinds of verb. Two of them are fixed ({مَبْنِيٌّ}) in every form.

blocks.html: Arabic has three kinds of verb. Two of them are fixed (مَبْنِيٌّ) in every form.

items.title: Past verb · fixed
items.text: An action that is done: {كَتَبَ} he wrote.

items.title: Present verb · mostly flexible
items.text: Its ending changes. We study it in Stage 8.

blocks.html:
Past verb · fixedالفِعْلُ المَاضِي
An action that is done: كَتَبَ he wrote.
Order verb · fixedفِعْلُ الأَمْرِ
Telling someone to act: اُكْتُبْ write!
Present verb · mostly flexibleالفِعْلُ المُضَارِعُ
Its ending changes. We study it in Stage 8.

data.text: In this unit we only use past and order verbs. Leave the present verb for later.

data.text: There are 14 persons but only 13 written forms. {كَتَبْتُمَا} is used for two men and for two women.

blocks.html: Tip: There are 14 persons but only 13 written forms. كَتَبْتُمَا is used for two men and for two women.

items.en: We did not go out of the house.
items.note: {مَا} before a past verb means "did not". See "Saying 'did not'" below.

blocks.html:
أَنَا ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى المَسْجِدِ.
I went to the mosque.
هِيَ جَلَسَتْ فِي الغُرْفَةِ.
She sat in the room.
نَحْنُ مَا خَرَجْنَا مِنَ البَيْتِ.
We did not go out of the house.
مَا before a past verb means "did not". See "Saying 'did not'" below.

data.text: Most endings of the past verb are attached pronouns. The pronoun is the doer. It is fixed, in the place of rafʿ ({فِي مَحَلِّ رَفْعٍ}).

data.title: The ـتْ of كَتَبَتْ is a ḥarf
data.text: In {كَتَبَتْ} the {ـتْ} only shows that the doer is feminine. It is a ḥarf, with no place. The doer is hidden: {هِيَ}.

blocks.html: The ـتْ of كَتَبَتْ is a ḥarf. In كَتَبَتْ the ـتْ only shows that the doer is feminine. It is a ḥarf, with no place. The doer is hidden: هِيَ.

items.title: Hidden doer
items.text: No ending. The doer is hidden: {هُوَ}.

items.title: Hidden doer
items.text: {ـتْ} is a ḥarf. The doer is hidden: {هِيَ}.

items.title: Attached doer
items.text: {ـتُ} is the doer, place of rafʿ.

blocks.html:
Hidden doerكَتَبَ
No ending. The doer is hidden: هُوَ.
Hidden doerكَتَبَتْ
ـتْ is a ḥarf. The doer is hidden: هِيَ.
Attached doerكَتَبْتُ
ـتُ is the doer, place of rafʿ.

data.text: When a noun is the doer, the verb has no doer ending: {كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ}. {الطَّالِبُ} is the doer.

blocks.html: Tip: When a noun is the doer, the verb has no doer ending: كَتَبَ الطَّالِبُ. الطَّالِبُ is the doer.

data.title: Fixed on fatha
data.text: {كَتَبَتْ} is built on fatha. The fatha is on the {ب}. The sukūn sits on the ḥarf {ـتْ}.

blocks.html: Fixed on fatha. كَتَبَتْ is built on fatha. The fatha is on the ب. The sukūn sits on the ḥarf ـتْ.

data.text: To say "did not", put {مَا} right before the past verb. The verb does not change at all: same form, same doer.

blocks.html: To say "did not", put مَا right before the past verb. The verb does not change at all: same form, same doer.

Past verbWith مَاMeaning

كَتَبَتْمَا كَتَبَتْshe did not write

data.title: مَا is a ḥarf of negation
data.text: This {مَا} means "not". It is a ḥarf: fixed, with no place ({لَا مَحَلَّ لَهُ مِنَ الإِعْرَابِ}). It does not change the verb after it.

blocks.html: مَا is a ḥarf of negation. This مَا means "not". It is a ḥarf: fixed, with no place (لَا مَحَلَّ لَهُ مِنَ الإِعْرَابِ). It does not change the verb after it.

items.en: I did not go to the market.
items.note: {ـتُ} is still the doer, in the place of rafʿ.

items.en: The student did not go out of the classroom.
We did not open the door.

items.ar: هَلْ كَتَبْتَ الدَّرْسَ؟ لَا، مَا كَتَبْتُهُ.
items.en: Did you write the lesson? No, I did not write it.
items.note: {لَا} is the answer "no". {مَا} makes the verb "did not".

blocks.html:
مَا ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى السُّوقِ.
I did not go to the market.
ـتُ is still the doer, in the place of rafʿ.
مَا خَرَجَ الطَّالِبُ مِنَ الفَصْلِ.
The student did not go out of the classroom.
مَا فَتَحْنَا البَابَ.
We did not open the door.
هَلْ كَتَبْتَ الدَّرْسَ؟ لَا، مَا كَتَبْتُهُ.
Did you write the lesson? No, I did not write it.
لَا is the answer "no". مَا makes the verb "did not".

data.text: Do not mix up two words that look the same. This {مَا} "not" is a ḥarf, with no place. The {مَا} "what" of unit 5 ({مَا هَذَا؟}) is an ism, and it has a place.

blocks.html: Tip: Do not mix up two words that look the same. This مَا "not" is a ḥarf, with no place. The مَا "what" of unit 5 (مَا هَذَا؟) is an ism, and it has a place.

data.text: You already know {لَا} "no". {لَا} also makes "don't…", but only with the present verb, later in the course. With the past verb we use {مَا}.

blocks.html: Tip: You already know لَا "no". لَا also makes "don't…", but only with the present verb, later in the course. With the past verb we use مَا.

data.title: Two ways to be built
data.text: {اُكْتُبْ} and {اُكْتُبْنَ} are built on sukūn. {اُكْتُبِي}، {اُكْتُبَا}، {اُكْتُبُوا} are built on dropping the {ن}. You will see where that {ن} comes from in Stage 8.

blocks.html: Two ways to be built. اُكْتُبْ and اُكْتُبْنَ are built on sukūn. اُكْتُبِي، اُكْتُبَا، اُكْتُبُوا are built on dropping the ن. You will see where that ن comes from in Stage 8.

اِجْلِسِي يَا آمِنَةُ.
Sit down, Aminah.
اُخْرُجُوا مِنَ الفَصْلِ.
Go out of the classroom (men).

data.text: A word cannot end in sukūn right before {ال}. So the sukūn becomes a small kasra. The verb is still fixed.

blocks.html: A word cannot end in sukūn right before ال. So the sukūn becomes a small kasra. The verb is still fixed.

items.en: The girl did not write the lesson.
items.note: {كَتَبَتْ} + {البِنْتُ}. The kasra sits on the ḥarf {ـتْ}. {مَا} changes nothing.

blocks.html:
اِفْتَحِ البَابَ.
Open the door.
اِفْتَحْ + البَابَ. Still built on sukūn.
مَا كَتَبَتِ البِنْتُ الدَّرْسَ.
The girl did not write the lesson.
كَتَبَتْ + البِنْتُ. The kasra sits on the ḥarf ـتْ. مَا changes nothing.

data.text: This kasra is only a bridge for speaking. It is not jarr and not iʿrāb.

blocks.html: Tip: This kasra is only a bridge for speaking. It is not jarr and not iʿrāb.

data.title: In short
items: Past and order verbs are fixed. The present verb is mostly flexible (Stage 8).
The past verb has 14 persons: {كَتَبَ} to {كَتَبْنَا}.
Endings like {ـتُ} {ـنَا} {ـُوا} are doer pronouns in the place of rafʿ. The {ـتْ} of {كَتَبَتْ} is a ḥarf.
Past: on fatha {كَتَبَ}, on damma {كَتَبُوا}, on sukūn {كَتَبْتُ}.
{مَا} + past verb is "did not": {مَا كَتَبَ}. This {مَا} is a ḥarf with no place.
Order: on sukūn {اُكْتُبْ} {اُكْتُبْنَ}, on dropping the {ن} {اُكْتُبِي} {اُكْتُبَا} {اُكْتُبُوا}.

blocks.html:
In short

  1. Past and order verbs are fixed. The present verb is mostly flexible (Stage 8).
  2. The past verb has 14 persons: كَتَبَ to كَتَبْنَا.
  3. Endings like ـتُ ـنَا ـُوا are doer pronouns in the place of rafʿ. The ـتْ of كَتَبَتْ is a ḥarf.
  4. Past: on fatha كَتَبَ, on damma كَتَبُوا, on sukūn كَتَبْتُ.
  5. مَا + past verb is "did not": مَا كَتَبَ. This مَا is a ḥarf with no place.
  6. Order: on sukūn اُكْتُبْ اُكْتُبْنَ, on dropping the ن اُكْتُبِي اُكْتُبَا اُكْتُبُوا.
  7. Middle damma gives اُ: اُدْرُسْ. Otherwise اِ: اِذْهَبْ.

examples.sentence: هَلْ كَتَبْتَ الدَّرْسَ؟ لَا، مَا كَتَبْتُهُ.
